title: Longest run of consecutive numbers
summary: Torn diary pages lie scattered; count the longest run of consecutive page numbers, starting only from pages whose previous page is missing.
goal: Find the longest run of consecutive page numbers

mapping.formal: Maximum count of x, x + 1, x + 2, …

examples.label: Ten pages
examples.explanation: Pages 0 to 8 are all there, with 0 twice.

ladder.name: Count up from every page
ladder.idea: For every page, count how many next pages exist by searching the whole list each time.

ladder.name: Sort, then scan
ladder.idea: Sort the page numbers and walk through, extending the run while each page is one more than the last.
ladder.insight: In sorted order, consecutive pages sit next to each other, so one pass finds every run.

ladder.name: Start only at run beginnings
ladder.idea: Put the pages in a set. Only from a page whose previous page is missing, count upwards while the next page exists.
ladder.insight: Counting from every page repeats the same runs. Starting only where a run begins means each page is counted once, and a set makes each check one step.

transfer.problem: From a list of employee badge numbers in no order, find the longest block of consecutive numbers that are all assigned.
transfer.explanation: Put the numbers in a set and count upward only from numbers whose predecessor is missing.

selfCheck: Uses a set for O(1) membership checks.
Starts counting only when x − 1 is missing.
